answer: In pregnancy eat iron-rich foods (spinach, jaggery, lentils), calcium sources (milk, curd, ragi) and take iron-folic acid tablets as advised by your health worker.
Iron-rich foods: green leafy vegetables, jaggery, dates, lentils, ragi. Eat them with vitamin C foods like lemon or amla to absorb more iron.
From 6 months, start with soft foods like mashed dal-rice, khichdi or ragi porridge, alongside breastfeeding. Add one new food at a time.
Good protein sources: dal, pulses, eggs, milk, curd, paneer, soybean, groundnuts. Combine cereals with pulses for better protein quality.
Vitamin A-rich foods: carrot, papaya, mango, pumpkin, drumstick leaves and spinach.
If a child cannot take milk, try curd or buttermilk (often better tolerated), ragi, sesame, and green leafy vegetables for calcium. Consult a doctor.
Signs of malnutrition in toddlers: low weight for age, thin arms, swelling of feet, tiredness, frequent infections. Visit the nearest Anganwadi or health centre.
One medium roti has roughly 70-100 kcal depending on size and oil/ghee used.
